chiral-wallpaper.look: All 17 groups render as crisp seamless tilings of the source (fbm source, chi=0.15). The hex groups are the showpiece: p6 is interlocking pinwheel blades with exact 6-fold rotation and no mirror lines, p3/p31m are triskelion tilings, p3m1/p6m/p4m are kaleidoscope mandalas. The pmm-family groups (p1..cmm) at this source scale read as streaky brocade tilings, distinct from each other but less striking. The chi sweep on p6 goes from the p6m snowflake kaleidoscope at 0 through pinwheels at 0.1 to swirling triskelions at 0.25 and spiral vortices at 0.5, all still exactly p6-symmetric. A worley source gives crisp Escher-like tile mosaics. Sheet: p6 fbm, FFT is a clean hex lattice of spots (periodic by construction), threshold shows hexagon-and-star tiles. Relief not meaningful (texture node). 3D vol: the fold applied to (x,y) with z passed to a 3D perlin gives a symmetric sponge whose every z slice has the group symmetry.
chiral-wallpaper.dims: 2D measured for all 17 groups; 3D measured as a prism (fold on x,y, z passed through), true cubic fold not written; 4D not written (plan: two 2D folds on (x,y) and (z,w))
chiral-wallpaper.range: Passes the source range through (p6 fbm sheet: -0.49..0.48). Domain modifier, no output scaling needed.
chiral-wallpaper.artifacts: Creases along K mirror lines (straight seams in hillshade for the pmm family); large chi adds extra folds (still symmetric, continuous); strict periodic repeat (axis 32); rectangular groups need DomainAxisScale for aspect
chiral-wallpaper.node_shape: ChiralWallpaper domain modifier: Group enum (17), Cell Size, Chirality (float, hybrid breaks exact symmetry), Modes int 1-4, Seed Offset for the warp table, Source
chiral-wallpaper.port_notes: Program-verified: invariance ~1e-5 under all coset reps and both lattice translations for every group, c0ratio 7.4-8.3, K-only mirrors broken (0.1-0.3) and in-group ones exactly 0. Construction: G tabulated as (K in {pmm,p4m,p6m}, lattice T, coset reps); v = Reynolds average of a T-periodic 4-mode trig field, RMS-normalised per group; folds are triU / triU+sort / hex lattice reduce + 2 rounds of abs-reflect60-reflect30-mirror x=1/2. The warp collapses to a table of (wave vector, phase, amplitude) sinusoids built when Group/Seed is set. Lattice sizes differ per group (pg 2x4, pmg 4x2, pgg 4x4, cm/cmm/p4g centred).

critic.notes: Keep. Exact, seamless, cheap, and nothing in the catalogue or a graph does it. Best in the hex chiral groups (p3, p31m, p6). Should be one node with domain-kaleidoscope's 2D groups: chi=0 already gives pmm, p4m and p6m, verified. Not terrain: hard periodic repeat and it reads as ornament. Gaps: 3D is only a prism (z through), no true 3D group fold, 4D not written so GenTileable is untested; hybrid Chirality breaks symmetry; hex tiles need a 1:sqrt3 rectangle for a pixel tile (reasoned, not tested). Worth a Remap in the preset because of the narrow range.
critic.improved: Added SoftFold: after the exact fold, each triangle edge pushes the point inward by sqrt(d^2+e^2)-d, so the normal derivative vanishes on the mirror. Being a function of K invariants it cannot change the group (17 of 17 rerun) and removes the straight seam lines. Lowered source detail from k=1.5 to k=1.0, which turns streaky brocade into readable motifs. Tried k=0.6: cleanest shapes but only 0.38 output range at seed 7, so backed off. Helped a lot on look and clean, nothing on terrain: the relief is a lattice of repeated craters.

tournament.notes: Exact, seamless, cheap, and no graph can do it because no existing node folds a domain. Black-box 17/17 on several configs (see answer). Coordinate map bounded at both step sizes for all groups. AVX2 port parity 4e-5: fold 0.15-0.18 ns rect and square, 0.98 hex; warp+fold 2.0 and 4.7 ns at 4 modes, source excluded. Best in p3, p31m, p6; p1 and p2 are hard to tell apart by eye. Not terrain: relief is a lattice of repeated craters. Gaps: 3D is only a prism, 4D not written, per-seed range narrow so a preset needs a Remap, Modes must be 2-4, chi=0 collapses 14 groups (that is the kaleidoscope mode). Should merge with domain-kaleidoscope's 2D groups.

master.one_liner: One-eval wallpaper-group domain: a Coxeter mirror fold plus an equivariant pre-warp reaches all 17 groups with no seams, including rotation-only pinwheels that plain folds cannot do.
master.look: Crisp tilings of any source. a=0 gives kaleidoscope mandalas. a>0 gives swirling pinwheels with no mirror lines (the p6 prototype looks like interlocking blades, Escher-like). Good for tiles, fabrics, parquet, sci-fi panels, alien terrain, masks. Prototyped: mode=0.
master.algorithm:
Problem: only 4 groups are pure mirror groups (pmm *2222, p4m *442, p3m1 *333, p6m *632). A fold into their triangle is C0 for any source. The other 13 have glued non-mirror edges, so folding them seams. Trick: F(p) = S( fold_K( p + a*v(p) ) ), where K is a Coxeter supergroup of the target group G and v is a G-equivariant, K-breaking vector field. If v(gp) = g v(p) for g in G then F(gp) = S(fold_K(g(p + a v(p)))) = F(p), since g is in K. F is continuous because fold_K and v are.
Building v: v_G(p) = sum over g in G/T of g^-1 v0(g p), for any T-periodic trig field v0 (Reynolds average). Store it as 2-6 sin/cos terms in a table computed when the enum is set. Shortcut: if psi is K-invariant, J*grad(psi) (J = rot90) is equivariant under rotations and anti-equivariant under mirrors, so it kills exactly the mirrors. p4 from p4m, mirrors at integers: psi = cos(pi x) + cos(pi y), v = (sin(pi y), -sin(pi x)). p6 from p6m with k in {(0,2/sqrt3),(1,1/sqrt3),(1,-1/sqrt3)}: grad = sum k_i sin(2 pi p.k_i), v = J grad. p3 from p3m1 with k in {(2/3,0),(1/3,1/sqrt3),(1/3,-1/sqrt3)}. pm from pmm: v = (0, cos(pi x)). pg uses a 2x1 sublattice with v_y = cos(pi x), v_x = cos(2 pi y). A psi that is anti-invariant under chosen mirrors keeps those mirrors instead, which gives p4g, p31m, cmm and so on.
Folds: pmm x=tri(x), y=tri(y). p4m adds (x,y)=(max,min). p3m1 and p6m: reduce by hex lattice, then 3-4 rounds of masked reflect across the 3 triangle lines (the prototype uses 12 rounds as a safe bound; a closed-form fold also works). Optional soft fold abs(x) -> sqrt(x^2+e^2) removes creases.
master.why_new: No symmetry node exists at all. A graph cannot reach this because reduction to the triangle needs masked reflections, and the chiral groups normally need seam hacks or several blended evals. This gets the whole 17-group enum with one source eval.
master.simd_plan: Enum picks a small coefficient table plus one of 4 fold routines, all floor/abs/min/max/Select. Cost is source + about 1 ns (p4m) to 3 ns (p6m), estimated. 3D: cubic C3~ fold (tri plus sort axes), chirality from an ABC-flow field (A sin z + C cos y, B sin x + A cos z, C sin y + B cos x). 4D: product of two 2D folds on (x,y) and (z,w), which keeps GenTileable working because it is a pure function of all 4 inputs.
master.continuity: C0 by construction, with creases along K mirrors; measured c0ratio 7.94 on p6 chi=.12. C1 with soft fold.
master.params: Group enum (17), Cell Size, Chirality (hybrid), Crease Softness, Source (GeneratorSource).
master.risks: Large Chirality makes the warp non-invertible: still continuous and still symmetric, but extra folds appear. Hybrid Chirality breaks exact symmetry (often desirable). Only p4, p6, p3 and p4m/p6m were looked at; the rest of the table is derived on paper. Rectangular groups need a DomainAxisScale for non-1:1 aspect. Closest related work is Farris's wallpaper functions from averaged waves.
master.cost_note: Cost is source + about 1 ns (p4m) to 3 ns (p6m), estimated.

bubble-invert.look: What the images show: with a stripe source each bubble is a clean butterfly dipole with the stripes continuing seamlessly across the rim (the grid col 1); with a checker, Apollonian-like nested checker dust inside round windows; with a cellular F1 source the bubbles become clusters of many small glossy cells inside the big cells, like frogspawn or compound eyes, and the hillshade is the best image of the family: foam within foam. With a 4-octave fbm source the bubbles are rough speckled patches (minification aliases the high octaves) and the relief is spiky, so the terrain use is poor; a low-frequency perlin source gives smooth hills with round blister mounds, odd but clean. Iteration 1 is clean; iterations 2-3 add scattered small nested bubbles that read as dust. 3D vol with stripes: sphere inversions punch round lens windows through the stripe slabs, so the 3D form works. Wide view shows the lattice at dens=0.8 (axis 27).

master.one_liner: Random non-overlapping circles or spheres where the domain is circle-inverted, so each bubble holds a mirrored, shrunken copy of the whole outside world, seamless at its rim.
master.look: Chrome-ball inclusions: rosettes and butterfly pairs set in otherwise untouched source. With stripes every bubble turns into a butterfly dipole; with a checker it shows nested fractal Apollonian-like dust; with fbm it reads as speckled star-shaped patches or geodes. Outside bubbles the source is unchanged, so it is a local embellishment for terrain, coral, geodes, alien ground, 3D foam voids. Prototyped: mode=2.
master.algorithm: Loop Iterations times: cell = floor(p). h = hash(cell). R = lerp(Rmin,Rmax,h1) with Rmax <= .5. c = cell + .5 + (.5-R)*(h2,h3), so the circle stays inside its cell and needs a 1x1 window. d2 = |p-c|^2. mask = d2 < R^2. p = Select(mask, c + (p-c)*R^2/max(d2, eps*R^2), p). Inversion is the identity on the circle, so no seam. After inversion the point is outside, and may land in another bubble on later iterations, nesting (Schottky/Kleinian group behaviour). eps caps magnification at 1/eps. Output S(p). Optional Density hash bit disables some bubbles.
master.why_new: Conformal, exact pointwise, isolated features with fractal interior at Value-noise cost. Domain warps cannot produce an interior that swaps inside and outside, and no existing node has this structure.
master.simd_plan: Per iteration: floor, 1 hash, 3 bit-field floats, compare, Select. About 1 ns per iteration (estimate), no window search, same in every dimension. Generic GenT over the pack, so 2D, 3D, 4D are all the same code.
master.continuity: C0 at rims, C-infinity inside; crease at rim. c0ratio 7.99 at iter=1 eps=.2. Steeper at iter=3 (4.03) from multiplied minification, not a jump.

master.risks: High minification means aliasing near the centre (bubble core looks like white noise at eps<.05). Keep eps >= .1 for building-block use. Lattice is visible if radii are large and density is high; pre-warp or a rotated second layer hides it. Source frequency also matters: a low-frequency source gives the clearest result.

fisk-meanders.look: Sheet: constant-width sinuous rivers in parallel belts, each bend a tangent-continuous biarc, so the centreline is smooth everywhere and bends vary from gentle to full goosenecks (omega loops with narrow necks) within one river. Oxbows are real: cut loops keep a shallower crescent lake while the live channel takes the straight neck chute (one or two per 8-unit window at pox=0.5). Scroll bars show as concentric arcs on the inner banks in gray and as fingerprint ridges in hillshade, but they stay subtle next to the channel depth. Older generations show as faint overprinted belts of the same geometry style. Relief: a flat plain with deep smooth trenches and faint ridged point bars inside the loops; readable as a floodplain, but the plain itself is dead flat (needs a base noise added in the graph). Wide view: the parallel strip structure is obvious (axis 8.4); warp=0.4 makes the belts wander and hides it. 3D vol: stacked independent channel layers crossfaded along z, honest but just stacked 2D.

fisk-meanders.artifacts: Parallel belts at wide view without an upstream warp; small gaps in the scroll-bar fingerprint within 0.15 Lc of bend ends and along a short radial line in tight loop cores (continuity fades); single-arc version was a uniform wave train; cost is the main flaw

master.one_liner: An analytic floodplain of tangent-continuous circular-arc rivers with real omega loops, oxbow lakes and concentric scroll bars, drawn in generations like the famous Mississippi meander maps.
master.look: Sinuous constant-width rivers with goosenecks, crescent lakes and fingerprint-like point-bar ridges, overprinted by faint abandoned belts. Nothing on the contact sheet resembles this. Good for floodplains, river masks, and map-like textures.
master.algorithm: Strips j=floor(v/S), each with one river along axis u. Breakpoints P_i=(i+jitter(i,j))*Lc on the strip axis (small lateral jitter). Per-strip half-sweep a=hash in [60,130] degrees, constant along a strip so tangents match; sign alternates by parity of i. Arc i: chord c=P_(i+1)-P_i, R=|c|/(2 sin a), centre=midpoint+sign*n*R*cos a. Distance: inside the sector (dot-product tests, no atan2) d=||q-centre|-R|, else min distance to endpoints. Oxbow: if hash(i,j)<pOx the live channel takes the straight chord and the arc becomes a plugged lake whose depth fades to 0 near its ends. Scroll bars: on the concave interior of the arc, add A*sin(2pi(R-|q-centre|)/lambda)*sectorFade*radialFade. Generations: for g=0..G-1 (oldest to youngest) use a different seed; h=lerp(h, -Depth*gamma^g*U(d/W), mask(d)), so younger channels cut older deposits.
master.why_new: Domain warp cannot make omega loops of constant width, because it stretches channels and would need multi-valued curves. Oxbows and scroll bars are explicit topology of this construction.
master.simd_plan: Branch free over a fixed window: 3 strips x 5 along-axis arcs (needed for a>90 deg) = 15 arc SDFs per generation, sqrt each. Estimate 8-10 ns per generation, 3 generations about 25-30 ns, about 25x Perlin and 7x CellularDistance. 3D: z is stratigraphic time with crossfaded seed layers (2x cost), which gives channel-belt deposits in vertical slices. 4D: same scheme; no torus tiling without periodic hashing along the strip.
master.continuity: C0 for depth via fade masks, with G1 river centrelines because all arcs in a strip share a. Overlapping neighbouring loops simply intersect, reading as cutoffs.
master.params: Strip Spacing, Bend Length, Sweep Min/Max (float), Width (hybrid), Oxbow Chance, Scroll Amp and Wavelength, Generations (int), Generation Gain, River Angle (float).

domain-kifs.look: Reserve idea, 3 renders. Sierpinski preset (Diagonal fold, s=2, N=3, Tile 4) with a cellular source: quadrants of the tile hold copies of the source at 1x, 2x, 4x scale, a nested-blocks mosaic with crisp mirror seams; with the 4-unit mirror tile the wide view is a hard square repeat (axis 11.5). The fold x N table with a 15 deg rotation and an fbm source shows concentric fan/arc bands around every tile centre for Orthant, Diagonal and Hex folds (the rotation about the fixed point dominates), and BoxSphere gives Mandelbox lace at N=2-4 that turns to pixel noise at N=6. Everything is continuous (c0ratio 8.0) and cheap, but it reads as a CG kaleidoscope with a visible centre, not as a texture or terrain anyone asked for; chiral-wallpaper covers the symmetric-tiling need with far better control.

master.one_liner: Kaleidoscopic IFS as a domain remap: N iterations of fold / rotate / scale-about-point, then sample the source; the detail is arranged self-similarly instead of summed like fBm.
master.look:
A fractal kaleidoscope: every triangle / square / tetrahedron of a self-similar subdivision contains an isometric copy of the source at its own scale. Terrain: nested plateaus and crystalline 'alien architecture'; caves (3D, Cellular or Perlin source inside a Mandelbox fold); textures: Sierpinski lace, Menger sponge tiles. Clearly different from FBm/Ridged, which spread detail uniformly.
[DomainFold, libs-modifiers] Look-tested (modes 9, 19). Mirror + rotate: lozenge carpet with soft quasi-tile symmetry. Sphere fold: dense ornate lace. Polar with 6 sectors: mandala. Log radial: recursive zoom into the centre. All unlike anything on the sheet, mostly for textures and stylised art rather than terrain.
master.algorithm:
Params: Iterations N (int 1..12), Scale s (>1), Offset o (per dim, hybrid ok), Angle (2D) or Yaw/Pitch (3D), Fold enum {Orthant, Diagonal, Hex, Icosa (3D), BoxSphere}, Normalise bool, CellSize.

  q = p / CellSize
  for i in 0..N-1:                               // uniform count
     q = Fold(q)
        Orthant:  q = Abs(q)
        Diagonal: q = Abs(q); conditional swaps so q.x >= q.y (>= q.z)
        Hex:      the 4-step D6 fold from DomainKaleidoscope
        Icosa:    the icosahedral reflection sequence (3D)
        BoxSphere (Mandelbox): q = Clamp(q,-1,1)*2 - q; r2 = Dot(q,q); q *= Select(r2 < 0.25, 4, Select(r2 < 1, 1/r2, 1))
     q = Rot(q)                                  // constant matrix from Angle/Yaw/Pitch
     q = q*s - o*(s-1)                           // scale about the fixed point o
  if Normalise: q *= s^-N                        // deepest-level features match CellSize
  return Source.Gen(seed, q)

Presets: Orthant, s=2, o=(1,1) => Sierpinski triangle partition; Diagonal, s=3, o=(1,1) => Sierpinski carpet / Menger in 3D; Icosa, s=2.0-2.6 => dodecahedral fractal shells; BoxSphere s=2-3 => Mandelbox cavities. Dimension agnostic (GenT over the pack).

[DomainFold, libs-modifiers] If TilePeriod > 0: p = T * abs(fract(p/T + 0.5)*2 - 1) (mirror tile, C0 and infinite). For i in 0..Iterations-1 by FoldType: Mirror: p = abs(p) - Offset. Polar (in a plane): r = |p.xy|; a = atan2poly(p.y, p.x); w = 2*pi/Sectors; a = mod(a, w); a = min(a, w - a); p.xy = r*(cos a, sin a) - Offset. Box: p = clamp(p, -L, L)*2 - p. Sphere: p *= 1 / clamp(|p|^2, Rmin^2, 1). Then p = Scale * R * p, with R a constant rotation. Log Radial option for Polar: (x,y) = (log r * K, a * K). Return Source(p).
master.why_new: The fractal nodes add detail everywhere; this one places detail with exact self-similar symmetry at a cost of roughly one Perlin per 6 iterations plus one source evaluation. There is no way to get hierarchical symmetric partitions from the current graph.
master.simd_plan: Per iteration <= 12 ops (Abs, FMA, Min/Max, Select, Reciprocal for BoxSphere); N=6 is ~70 ops (about one Perlin 2D); one source eval; no lattice; identical code 2D/3D/4D with a per-dimension Fold specialisation.
master.continuity: C0: Abs and conditional swaps are continuous; the BoxSphere piecewise scale is continuous at r2=0.25 (4 = 1/0.25) and r2=1 (1 = 1). Creases at every fold plane at every level.
master.params: Iterations int, Scale float, Offset per-dim hybrid (noise-driven offset gives a 'warped KIFS' that stays continuous), Angle / Yaw / Pitch float, Fold enum, Normalise bool, Cell Size float.
master.risks:
Strong 'CG fractal' signature can dominate; high N shrinks features past pixel size (aliasing). A noisy hybrid Offset is amplified by s per iteration, so document that. Offsets near 0 collapse to a plain kaleidoscope.
[DomainFold, libs-modifiers] Non-stationary unless Tile Period is set: far from origin Mirror folds act as a plain translation, and there is a visible centre. Magnifying folds alias fast. Effective source frequency shifts, so Feature Scale feels different. Polynomial atan2 accuracy at the sector seam matters. Low use for terrain, so priority depends on whether stylised textures matter.
master.cost_note: Per iteration <= 12 ops (Abs, FMA, Min/Max, Select, Reciprocal for BoxSphere); N=6 is ~70 ops (about one Perlin 2D); one source eval; no lattice; identical code 2D/3D/4D with a per-dimension Fold specialisation.
master.variant_notes: DomainFold adds tile folding (infinite, stationary), polar sectors and a log-radial Droste option.
